title: UK public sector finances, November 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the last borrowing print before the OBR's Budget-day monthly profiles arrive, and it lands on the 22nd, not the usual 19th-21st
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/publicsectorfinancesuknovember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the publisher's own release-calendar entry reads 'Public sector finances, UK: November 2026', '22 December 2026 at 7:00am', describing the headline measures of net borrowing, net cash requirement and net debt, and marked 'This release is not yet published.' Corroborated by publication-cadence arithmetic on the ONS's own bulletin index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk, fetched direct 2026-09-09): 137 consecutive PSF bulletins from 2015-04-23 to 2026-08-21 all fall on the 19th-26th, and the November-edition bulletins have printed on 2020-12-22, 2021-12-21, 2022-12-21, 2023-12-21, 2024-12-20 and 2025-12-19. Filed estimate on the confirmed-prefix taxonomy's lack of an ONS slot and this lane's no-self-confirm limit; the date is the publisher's own and is not in doubt. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-public-sector-finances-2026-11-20, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-public-sector-finances-2026-11-20 LANE, 2026-09-09. It earns a slot for one reason the proposing lane measured rather than assumed. That lane's central finding is that the ONS does not re-benchmark its 'versus forecast' comparisons on Budget day but on the day the OBR's MONTHLY PROFILES land, which its own two most recent precedents put at D+84 (Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 -> first use in the bulletin published 2025-01-22) and D+86 (Autumn Budget 2025-11-26 -> ONS states verbatim that the new profiles 'will be used to inform our Public Sector Finances, UK January 2026 statistical bulletin on 20 February 2026'). 2026-10-28 plus 85 days is 2027-01-21. This 2026-12-22 print is therefore the LAST outturn still measured against the pre-Budget 'Economic and fiscal outlook - March 2026' profile, and the one after it is the switch — which makes this the control observation for that lane's FT-1 and the boundary a later pulse has to watch. A second, smaller reason: the date is the 22nd, outside the 19th-21st band five of the last six November-edition prints used, so a calendar that guessed the cadence would have guessed wrong. Tiered LOW on the proposer's own measured null across 137 PSF release days since 2015-04-23: IGLT.L 1.07x an ordinary day (Welch t = 0.70), GBP/USD 0.92x, US 10-year 0.89x, S&P 500 0.95x, VIX 0.94x, FTSE 100 0.83x (t = -2.30, significantly quieter). symbols: [], no fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook, no UK-listed name tracked. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
